\begin{document}
Graph neural networks extend convolutional ideas to irregular, relational domains.
Instead of a fixed grid, each node aggregates messages from its neighbours,
so the same parameters are reused across graphs of very different sizes.

Deep stacks of message passing layers suffer from oversmoothing.
After enough rounds every node embedding converges to almost the same vector,
which destroys the discriminative power of the representation.

We study residual connections and normalisation schemes that delay this collapse,
and we measure their effect on citation networks and molecular property benchmarks.
\end{document}
